Plot the expected value of perfect information

plot.voipred_evpi.Rd

The plot of results of evpi(): EVPI (or relative EVPI) against the threshold, for one or more results, e.g. for different validation samples or sets of models; or, for one result, P(useful) or P(best) from the same draws (as plot.voipred_p_useful() and plot.voipred_p_best() draw them). To draw EVPI under the decision curve, use plot(<nb_val result>, evpi = ) (plot.voipred_nb()).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evpi'
plot(
  x,
  ...,
  type = c("evpi", "relative", "p_useful", "p_best"),
  labels = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  per = getOption("voipred.per", 1),
  interactive = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A result of evpi().

...

More results of evpi() to draw on the same plot. A result given here with a name is labelled with its name.

type

"evpi" (default), "relative" (relative EVPI, with a dashed line at 1; infinite values are left out), "p_useful" (P(useful) of each model) or "p_best" (P(best) of each strategy); the last two for one result.

labels

Optional names of the curves, one per result, in order (type = "p_useful": one per model). Default: "EVPI" for one result, the argument names (or "EVPI 1", "EVPI 2", ...) for several.

colors

Optional colours of the curves, instead of the defaults: named by curve label, or unnamed, one per curve in order (with type = "p_useful" or "p_best", as in plot.voipred_p_useful() and plot.voipred_p_best()).

per

Scale of EVPI (type = "evpi"): the number of patients it is expressed per. Default 1 (per patient); e.g. per = 100000, and the y axis says "(per 100,000 patients)". Relative EVPI, P(useful) and P(best) have no unit. The default can be set with options(voipred.per = ).

interactive

TRUE for an interactive plot (needs the plotly package). Default FALSE.

Value

A ggplot object, or a plotly widget with interactive = TRUE.

See also

evpi(), plot.voipred_nb()

Examples

df_dev_binary <- gusto[1:5000, ]
df_val_binary <- gusto[5001:5500, ]
fit <- glm(day30 ~ age + Killip + sysbp + pulse,
           family = binomial, data = df_dev_binary)
df_val_binary$p <- predict(fit, newdata = df_val_binary, type = "response")
res <- nb_val(data = df_val_binary,
              predicted_risk = df_val_binary$p,
              outcome = "day30",
              thresholds = seq(0.01, 0.3, by = 0.01))
set.seed(1)
e <- evpi(res, n_sim = 500)
plot(e)

plot(e, type = "relative")

plot(e, type = "p_useful")

plot(e, type = "p_best")
